The dust in the attic tasted like forgotten time. Seven-year-old Leo sat cross-legged on the floorboards, surrounded by a fortress of cardboard boxes and moth-eaten coats. He wasn’t looking for treasure, not really. He was looking for something to do while the rain hammered against the windowpane, a rhythmic drumming that usually lulled him to sleep. But today, his eyes were wide, fixed on a leather-bound tome that had fallen from the highest shelf. It was thick, its spine cracked like dry earth, and it smelled of vanilla and decay.

Leo opened it carefully. The pages were brittle, yellowed at the edges, filled with dense, archaic text he couldn’t read. He flipped through chapters on botany and celestial navigation, his fingers tracing the faded ink. Then, near the back, his hand stopped. Tucked between two pages was a sheet of parchment, folded into a perfect square. It was lighter than the rest of the book, fragile as a whisper.
